payload.task_text:
Our operations team needs a report on how well we are meeting our service level agreements for customer support tickets. Please pull the ticket data from our data warehouse along with the SLA policy definitions, and determine for each priority level how many tickets met the response time target versus how many did not. The data warehouse contains a support center database with tables for tickets, SLA policies, and agents.

Create an Excel file called SLA_Compliance_Report.xlsx in the workspace with two sheets. The first sheet should be named "Compliance" and should have columns Priority, Total_Tickets, Avg_Response_Hours (rounded to two decimal places), SLA_Target_Hours, Compliant_Count (number of tickets where the response time was at or below the SLA response target), and Compliance_Rate (percentage of compliant tickets rounded to two decimal places). Sort rows by SLA_Target_Hours ascending. Note that only priorities appearing in the actual ticket data should be included, so if a priority level defined in the SLA policy has zero tickets, omit it.

The second sheet should be named "Summary" with columns Metric and Value. Include the following rows: Total_Tickets (the grand total across all priorities), Overall_Compliance_Rate (percentage across all tickets, rounded to two decimal places), Worst_Priority (the priority with the lowest compliance rate), and Best_Priority (the priority with the highest compliance rate).

After creating the report, send an email to ops-manager@company.com with subject "SLA Compliance Report Summary" containing the overall compliance rate and the worst performing priority in the body text.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, the main agent must complete it directly and must not dispatch a sub-agent. Inspect the ticket and SLA-policy schemas, then issue one server-side join/aggregate by exact priority. Count a ticket compliant only when response_time_hours <= policy response target, omit policy priorities with zero tickets, retain raw compliant/total counts, compute per-priority and overall 0-100 rates from those counts, rank worst/best by raw rate with an alphabetical tie-break, and sort rows by target hours ascending. Stop if any observed ticket priority has no matching policy.

Resolve the real task workspace dynamically and create SLA_Compliance_Report.xlsx once with exact Compliance and Summary sheets/headers, literal numeric cells and requested rounding. Read both populated ranges back. Search all Sent-mail pages for the exact recipient ops-manager@company.com and subject SLA Compliance Report Summary, read candidates to confirm the recipient, send once only when absent, include the frozen overall rate and worst priority, and read the retained message back. Perform one final arithmetic and identity check without delegation or a repair wave.

nodes.text:
Plan the following task and return an ordered subtask list with dispatch decisions (self / explore / coder) and dependencies.

TASK: The operations team needs an SLA compliance report for customer support tickets.

1. Pull ticket data from the data warehouse (Snowflake) — there is a support center database with tables for tickets, SLA policies, and agents. Explore the databases/schemas/tables to find the relevant tables (likely named tickets, sla_policies, agents). Understand the schema: ticket response time (created_at vs first_response_at or similar), priority field, SLA target per priority (from sla policies table).

2. Compute for each priority level: total tickets, average response hours (rounded to 2 decimals), SLA target hours, compliant count (tickets where response time <= SLA target), compliance rate (percentage rounded to 2 decimals). Only include priorities that appear in actual ticket data (omit SLA policy priorities with zero tickets).

3. Create an Excel file SLA_Compliance_Report.xlsx in the workspace directory /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-sf-ticket-sla-compliance/workspace with two sheets:
   - Sheet "Compliance": columns Priority, Total_Tickets, Avg_Response_Hours (2dp), SLA_Target_Hours, Compliant_Count, Compliance_Rate (2dp). Sorted by SLA_Target_Hours ascending.
   - Sheet "Summary": columns Metric, Value with rows: Total_Tickets (grand total), Overall_Compliance_Rate (2dp), Worst_Priority (lowest compliance rate), Best_Priority (highest compliance rate).

4. Send an email to ops-manager@company.com with subject "SLA Compliance Report Summary" containing the overall compliance rate and the worst performing priority in the body.

Note: file workspace root is /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-sf-ticket-sla-compliance/workspace

Your job: inspect the available data (read-only) if useful, and produce an ordered plan specifying for each subtask: the dispatch decision (self/explore/coder), and whether it is parallelizable or must wait on another subtask. Keep it concise and actionable.
Plan SLA compliance report task

Create an Excel file at this exact path:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-sf-ticket-sla-compliance/workspace/SLA_Compliance_Report.xlsx

Use the mcp__excel__* tools (create_workbook, create_worksheet / rename_worksheet, write_data_to_excel, get_workbook_metadata, read_data_from_excel) to build the workbook. The file must contain exactly two sheets with the following content. Values are already computed — do NOT re-query Snowflake.

Sheet 1 — name: "Compliance"
Columns (row 1 headers): Priority, Total_Tickets, Avg_Response_Hours, SLA_Target_Hours, Compliant_Count, Compliance_Rate
Data rows (already sorted by SLA_Target_Hours ascending):
- High, 6466, 6.23, 4, 778, 12.03
- Medium, 15774, 12.28, 8, 1645, 10.43
- Low, 9348, 25.76, 24, 4204, 44.97
Avg_Response_Hours values are rounded to 2 decimal places; Compliance_Rate values are percentages rounded to 2 decimal places (write the numeric value, e.g. 12.03 meaning 12.03%).

Sheet 2 — name: "Summary"
Columns (row 1 headers): Metric, Value
Rows:
- Total_Tickets, 31588
- Overall_Compliance_Rate, 20.98
- Worst_Priority, Medium
- Best_Priority, Low

Notes:
- The workbook created by create_workbook typically contains a default sheet (e.g. "Sheet1") — rename it to "Compliance" or delete it and create the two sheets so the final workbook has EXACTLY the two sheets "Compliance" and "Summary" (in that order if possible).
- Write headers + data starting at A1.
- After writing, verify by calling get_workbook_metadata (confirm 2 sheets with correct names) and read_data_from_excel on both sheets to confirm all values are present and correct.

Report back: the final sheet names in order, and confirmation that all values were written correctly.
Build SLA compliance Excel report
